expert_diagnosis: Hertz's crisis was caused by an external demand shock (COVID-19) meeting a structurally vulnerable balance sheet — high leverage, large fleet-financing obligations, and a fixed-cost model with no revenue buffer. The company had insufficient liquidity to absorb a prolonged demand collapse without formal restructuring. Root causes: cash liquidity crisis, travel demand collapse from COVID-19, pre-existing debt and fleet-financing pressure, high fixed-cost structure, and external shock incompatible with existing capital structure.
expert_first_action: Immediate cash preservation and creditor engagement; pursue formal Chapter 11 restructuring to obtain automatic stay and restructure fleet-financing; optimize fleet disposition at best available prices; plan for multiple demand-recovery scenarios; preserve core operating capabilities, brand, and workforce.
actual_decision: Hertz filed voluntary Chapter 11 on 22 May 2020.
harmful_actions: Pre-crisis high leverage left no buffer for external shock
Fleet-financing structure created rigid obligations incompatible with sudden revenue collapse
beneficial_actions: Chapter 11 filing obtained automatic stay and restructuring framework
Plan of reorganization eliminated over $5 billion in debt
Post-reorganization global liquidity of over $2.2 billion secured
Company emerged from Chapter 11 with a stronger balance sheet
citation: Hertz SEC-filed Chapter 11 press release, exhibit 99-1; Hertz official reorganization confirmation press release: plan confirmed, creditors paid in full; Kroll bankruptcy administration records
actual_outcome: Hertz filed voluntary Chapter 11 on 22 May 2020. Plan of reorganization confirmed by bankruptcy court. Eliminated over $5 billion in debt. Provided over $2.2 billion global liquidity. Hertz emerged from Chapter 11 with a stronger balance sheet and creditors paid in full.
documented_root_causes: Cash liquidity crisis — collapsed revenue insufficient to service obligations
Travel demand collapse — COVID-19 near-total revenue destruction
Debt and fleet-financing pressure — large contractual obligations persisting through demand collapse
High fixed-cost structure — costs did not flex with revenue
External shock from COVID-19 travel collapse — exogenous cause meeting structural vulnerability
Need for formal restructuring — only mechanism to restructure contractual obligations
final_business_state: Emerged from Chapter 11 as restructured entity. Over $5 billion debt eliminated. Over $2.2 billion global liquidity. Creditors paid in full.
